notes: Must be the first effective statement when present.
Omitting it creates an anonymous module; no default name is derived from the filename or path.
The explicit name is used by name-based lookup APIs: host Execute/GetMethod/GetModule and script global.getModule.
Import/include resolution and runtime module identity use the resolved ScriptSourceReference.FullPath.
Only explicit names participate in module-name conflict checks.
Must appear at the top of the module.
Must appear at the top of the module.

features.syntax: export func name() { } | export var name = value; | export const name = value;
notes: Invalid outside module scope.
May shadow an outer var in a child block.
Duplicate declaration in the same scope is rejected.
Cannot be assigned after declaration.
A child block may not redeclare a visible outer const.

features.syntax: var { a, b } = obj; var [ first, ...rest ] = array;
notes: Initializer is required.

features.syntax: @global(); declare var name; declare const name;
notes: Only valid in @global() declaration files.
Optional compile-time host global contract; host globals still resolve at runtime without it.
No runtime module property or initialization code is emitted.
The declared name must be a single identifier with no initializer or destructuring pattern.
Reads and writes resolve through global unless shadowed by a local variable.
declare const participates in compile-time const assignment checks.
@global() files cannot be imported or included and are not compiled as modules.
Only valid in @global() declaration files.
Optional compile-time host global contract; host globals still resolve at runtime without it.
No function body or runtime module property is emitted.
Function overloads are not allowed; duplicate global declarations are rejected across the project.

features.syntax: @global(); declare type Name { static func member(); constructor(args); TypeName field; }
notes: Only valid in @global() declaration files.
Editor-only script contract for an [AuroraNativeType]; member signatures are not used for compiler inference.
Do not use declare class, declare module, or a structural type declaration for host Types.
Static-only Types omit constructor and mark members static; at most one constructor describes a constructible Type.
Application native types are selected with CompilerOptionsBuilder.WithNativeTypes; Math, JSON, TDoc, console, Conv8, and HotPatch are always available.
typeof of these globals is "type"; new fails when the Type has no exported constructor.

features.syntax: type Point { Number x; Number y; } | export type Point { Number x; Number y; }
notes: Compile-time object shape for native field derivation.
Not a host NativeType contract and not a runtime structure check.
Fields only; constructors and methods belong on declare type, not on type.

features.syntax: context name; | context name as NativeType;
notes: Module-level alias for the current ScriptContext.UserState instance, not a field of a session bag.
Multiple context names are allowed; each is a separate binding that still names the same UserState object.
as Type must be a public host NativeType from WithNativeTypes. Each typed name is loaded once per function into a typed local (ldfld UserState + castclass) and then uses native fields and calls.
An untyped context stays dynamic. A function may use several context names at once; each is cached independently.
A native function whose return contract is that NativeType returns the CLR type from $native. Proven call sites keep the instance; only $typed converts to ScriptDatum.
Context names cannot be exported and cannot collide with other module declarations. Parameters and locals of the same name shadow the context.
function is also accepted as a keyword.

features.syntax: func name(int32 value) int32 { ... } | value as int32 | type Shape { int32 field; }
notes: int32 is a lowercase numeric constraint, not a script runtime type or global constructor.
It accepts only finite integral Number values in -2147483648..2147483647, rejects negative zero, and never truncates or wraps at a checked boundary.

A local whose every assignment is an integer (integer literals, int32 parameters/fields/returns, Int32Array elements, signed bitwise results, and +/-/*/% over those) keeps 32-bit storage and wraps like CLR int instead of being widened to Number.
Expressions built from those locals also wrap: currentX - 1 stays int32 and is passed to an int32 parameter without a Number round-trip.
Integer storage cannot hold negative zero or NaN, so -14 % 7 is 0 and an integer remainder by zero raises a runtime error; give an operand Number storage to keep script remainder semantics.
/ remains Number division. An exact integer quotient uses ((a - b) / c) as int32; parentheses are required because as binds tighter than /.
Native/direct parameters and returns use CLR System.Int32; dynamic boundaries perform an exact range and integrality check.
Values retain Number identity, so typeof remains "number".

features.syntax: func name(uint32 value) uint32 { ... } | value as uint32 | type Shape { uint32 field; } | 0xD76AA478u
notes: uint32 is a lowercase numeric constraint, not a script runtime type or global constructor.
It accepts only finite integral Number values in 0..4294967295, rejects negative zero, and never truncates or wraps at a checked boundary.
U/u suffixes select UInt32 literal storage; unsuffixed literal inference is unchanged.
Native/direct parameters and returns use CLR System.UInt32, while UInt32Array element reads preserve the same scalar flow type.
Arithmetic wraps modulo 2^32, bitwise results remain UInt32, and >> is a logical right shift.
Values retain Number identity, so typeof remains "number".

features.syntax: native func name(parameters) void { statements; return; }
notes: void is a contextual return contract for native functions only; it is not an alias for Null.
The native CLR entry returns void. Falling through and bare return are valid; return expression is rejected.
Direct native calls used as statements do not materialize a result.
Exported, dynamic, or otherwise value-producing calls observe null.
void is invalid on ordinary functions, parameters, fields, and type assertions.

features.syntax: export native func name() NativeType { return typedContext; }
notes: A declared host NativeType return is the CLR type on the $native entry, not ScriptDatum.
Proven script and host call sites invoke NativeType members without FromObject/ToObject round trips.
The $typed shell still returns ScriptDatum for Execute, unproven calls, and escaped function values.
The host is responsible for supplying a matching UserState; a mismatch throws InvalidCastException at the context load.

features.syntax: x => x + 1; (a, b = 1) => { return a + b; }
notes: Expression body is lowered to return expression.
Interpolations evaluate left to right.
Compiler selects concat or StringBuilder strategy by element count.
Returns an interned type-name string.
Primitives and privileged kinds use lowercase names: null, boolean, number, string, object, array, date, regex, function, type, error, clr:function, clr:bonding.

Native objects stored as ValueKind.Object report constructor names: Int8Array, UInt8Array, Int16Array, UInt16Array, Int32Array, UInt32Array, Int64Array, UInt64Array, Float32Array, Float64Array, BooleanArray, StringBuffer, HashMap, Path.
Infrastructure NativeTypes (Math, JSON, TDoc, console, Conv8, HotPatch) and host NativeTypes report "type".
Do not add ValueKind members for new native types; override ScriptObject.TypeOfValue instead.
check TypeName value is a separate exact runtime assertion used by the typed backend.
Constructs a TDoc value directly inside an AuroraScript expression.
Object members use optional readonly and type-name prefixes followed by a static property name and value.
Only value positions accept $(expression); property names and type names are static.
Standalone .tdoc documents omit the tdoc prefix and do not allow interpolation.
Host NativeTypes listed in WithNativeTypes that implement INativeTypedDocument can be used as TypeName; the engine constructs the native ScriptObject directly.

INativeTypedDocument.WriteTypedDocument chooses an object body (WriteMember), an array body (WriteElement), or a scalar body (WriteValue for null, boolean, number, or string). INativeTypedDocument.ReadTypedDocument reads those shapes through TypedDocumentInput.
Dynamic ScriptObject properties are excluded unless that NativeType opts in with WriteDynamicMembers and DefineDynamicMember; those helpers require an object body.

features.syntax: for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) statement
notes: Condition expression is required.
Iterates arrays, objects, and strings according to runtime iterator behavior.
Catch variable creates a catch scope.
Use stringAndRelease for pooled builder return.
